# Overview

This template extracts the visible Python code used to produce an analogue of Figure 1 from Ball and Brown (1968). The focus is on a runnable workflow rather than on the fuller book chapter discussion.

:::{.callout-tip}
This document assumes that you have:

1. created a local `.venv` with `uv sync`
2. created a local `.env` file with `WRDS_ID` and `DATA_DIR`
3. downloaded the required WRDS tables as Parquet files using `db2pq`
:::

```{python}
import io
import re
import zipfile

import polars as pl
import requests

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from era_pl import load_parquet, NumberedLines, plotnine_star as p9

load_dotenv()
```

:::{.callout-note}
The package imported here as `era_pl` is installed from PyPI as `era-py`.
:::

## Load WRDS data

The code below expects local Parquet versions of the following WRDS tables:

- `crsp.msi`
- `crsp.msf`
- `crsp.stocknames`
- `crsp.ccmxpf_lnkhist`
- `comp.funda`
- `comp.fundq`

```{python}
msi = load_parquet("msi", "crsp")
msf = load_parquet("msf", "crsp")
ccmxpf_lnkhist = load_parquet("ccmxpf_lnkhist", "crsp")
stocknames = load_parquet("stocknames", "crsp")

funda = load_parquet("funda", "comp")
fundq = load_parquet("fundq", "comp")
```

:::{.callout-note}
These objects are `pl.LazyFrame` objects, so Polars delays the actual work until a later step such as `.collect()`.
:::

## Announcement dates and return windows

```{python}
#| label: annc_events
annc_events = (
    fundq
    .filter(
        pl.col("indfmt") == "INDL",
        pl.col("datafmt") == "STD",
        pl.col("consol") == "C",
        pl.col("popsrc") == "D",
        pl.col("fqtr") == 4,
        pl.col("fyr") == 12,
        pl.col("rdq").is_not_null()
    )
    .select("gvkey", "datadate", "rdq")
    .with_columns(annc_month=pl.col("rdq").dt.truncate("1mo"))
)
```

```{python}
#| label: crsp_dates
crsp_dates = (
    msi
    .select("date")
    .sort("date")
    .with_row_index("td", offset=1)
    .with_columns(
        td=pl.col("td").cast(pl.Int32),
        month=pl.col("date").dt.truncate("1mo"),
    )
)
```

```{python}
#| label: annc_months
annc_months = (
    crsp_dates
    .select(
        pl.col("month").alias("annc_month"),
        pl.col("td").alias("annc_td"),
    )
    .with_columns(
        start_td=pl.col("annc_td") - 11,
        end_td=pl.col("annc_td") + 6,
    )
)
```

```{python}
#| label: td_link
td_link = (
    crsp_dates
    .join(annc_months, how="cross")
    .filter(pl.col("td").is_between(pl.col("start_td"),
                                    pl.col("end_td")))
    .with_columns(rel_td=pl.col("td") - pl.col("annc_td"))
    .select("annc_month", "rel_td", "date")
)
```

```{python}
#| label: ccm_link
ccm_link = (
    ccmxpf_lnkhist
    .filter(
        pl.col("linktype").is_in(["LC", "LU", "LS"]),
        pl.col("linkprim").is_in(["C", "P"])
    )
    .with_columns(
        permno=pl.col("lpermno"),
        linkenddt=pl.col("linkenddt").fill_null(pl.col("linkenddt").max()),
    )
    .select("gvkey", "permno", "linkdt", "linkenddt")
)
```

```{python}
events_linked = (
    annc_events
    .join(td_link, on="annc_month", how="inner")
    .join(ccm_link, on=["gvkey"], how="inner")
    .filter(pl.col("annc_month").is_between(pl.col("linkdt"),
                                            pl.col("linkenddt")))
)
```

```{python}
#| label: rets_all
#| cache: false
rets_all = (
    events_linked
    .join(msf.select("permno", "date", "ret", "prc", "shrout"),
          on=["permno", "date"], how="inner")
    .join(
        stocknames
        .filter(pl.col("exchcd").is_in([1, 2, 3]))
        .select("permno", "namedt", "nameenddt"),
        on="permno",
        how="inner",
    )
    .filter(pl.col("date").is_between(pl.col("namedt"),
                                      pl.col("nameenddt")))
    .select("gvkey", "datadate", "rel_td", "permno", "date", "ret")
    .filter(pl.col("datadate").dt.year().is_between(1987, 2002))
)
```

```{python}
#| label: full_panel
#| cache: false
rets_counts = (
    rets_all
    .group_by("gvkey", "datadate")
    .agg(n_obs=pl.col("ret").count())
)

full_panel = (
    rets_counts
    .with_columns(max_n_obs=pl.col("n_obs").max())
    .filter(pl.col("n_obs") == pl.col("max_n_obs"))
    .select("gvkey", "datadate")
)
```

```{python}
#| label: rets
#| cache: false
rets = (
    rets_all
    .join(full_panel, on=["gvkey", "datadate"], how="inner")
)
```

## Size-adjusted benchmark returns

The template uses size-adjusted returns based on files from Ken French's data library.

:::{.callout-note}
`NumberedLines()` is a convenience wrapper for locating sections of the downloaded text file without hard-coding line numbers.
:::

```{python}
def zip_url_to_text(url):
    resp = requests.get(url)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    zf = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(resp.content))
    inner_name = zf.namelist()[0]
    raw = zf.read(inner_name).decode("latin1")
    return NumberedLines(raw.splitlines())
```

```{python}
url = ("https://mba.tuck.dartmouth.edu/pages/faculty/ken.french/ftp/"
       "Portfolios_Formed_on_ME_CSV.zip")

text = zip_url_to_text(url)
```

```{python}
vw_start_regex = re.compile(r"Value Weight.*Monthly")
vw_start = text.filter(vw_start_regex).index[0] + 1

vw_end_regex = re.compile(r"Equal Weight.*Monthly")
vw_end = text.filter(vw_end_regex).index[0]
vw_lines = text[vw_start:vw_end].reset_index()

ew_end_regex = re.compile(r"^\s+Value Weight.*Annual")
ew_end = text.filter(ew_end_regex).index[0]
ew_start = vw_end + 1
ew_lines = text[ew_start:ew_end].reset_index()
```

```{python}
def lines_to_df(lines, header="infer"):
    block = "\n".join(lines)
    has_header = header == "infer"

    df_raw = pl.read_csv(
        io.StringIO(block),
        has_header=has_header,
    )

    value_cols = df_raw.columns[1:]

    df_raw = df_raw.with_columns(
        pl.col(value_cols)
        .cast(pl.String)
        .str.strip_chars()
        .replace("-99.99", None)
        .cast(pl.Float64)
    )

    return df_raw.rename({df_raw.columns[0]: "date"})
```

```{python}
def read_data(lines):
    return (
        lines_to_df(lines)
        .lazy()
        .with_columns(
            month=(pl.col("date").cast(pl.String) + "01")
            .str.strptime(pl.Date, format="%Y%m%d", strict=False)
        )
        .drop("date")
        .unpivot(index="month", variable_name="quantile", value_name="ret")
        .with_columns(
            ret=pl.col("ret") / 100.0,
            decile=(
                pl.when(pl.col("quantile") == "Hi 10").then(pl.lit(10))
                .when(pl.col("quantile") == "Lo 10").then(pl.lit(1))
                .when(pl.col("quantile").str.contains("-Dec"))
                .then(
                    pl.col("quantile")
                    .str.replace("-Dec", "")
                    .cast(pl.Int32, strict=False)
                )
                .otherwise(None)
            ),
        )
        .filter(pl.col("decile").is_not_null())
        .select("month", "ret", "decile")
        .sort(["month", "decile"])
    )
```

```{python}
ew_rets = read_data(ew_lines)
vw_rets = read_data(vw_lines)
```

```{python}
size_rets = (
    ew_rets
    .select("month", "decile", pl.col("ret").alias("ew_ret"))
    .join(
        vw_rets
        .select("month", "decile", pl.col("ret").alias("vw_ret")),
        on=["month", "decile"],
        how="inner",
    )
    .sort(["month", "decile"])
)
```

```{python}
url_bp = ("https://mba.tuck.dartmouth.edu/pages/faculty/ken.french/ftp/"
          "ME_Breakpoints_CSV.zip")

text = zip_url_to_text(url_bp)
```

```{python}
#| label: me_breakpoints
#| cache: false
me_last = text.filter(re.compile(r"^Copyright")).index[0]

df_raw = lines_to_df(text[1:me_last], header=None)
df_raw.columns = ["month", "n"] + [f"p{i}" for i in range(5, 101, 5)]
```

```{python}
me_breakpoints_raw = (
    df_raw
    .with_columns(
        month=(pl.col("month").cast(pl.String) + "01")
        .str.strptime(pl.Date, format="%Y%m%d", strict=False)
    )
    .select(["month"] + [f"p{i}" for i in range(10, 101, 10)])
    .unpivot(index="month", variable_name="decile", value_name="cutoff")
    .with_columns(
        decile=(
            pl.col("decile")
            .str.slice(1)
            .cast(pl.Int32, strict=False) / 10
        ).cast(pl.Int32)
    )
    .select("month", "decile", "cutoff")
    .sort("month", "decile")
    .lazy()
)
```

```{python}
me_breakpoints = (
    me_breakpoints_raw
    .sort(["month", "decile"])
    .with_columns(
        me_min=pl.col("cutoff").shift(1).over("month").fill_null(0),
        me_max=pl.when(pl.col("decile") == 10)
        .then(float("inf"))
        .otherwise(pl.col("cutoff")),
    )
    .drop("cutoff")
    .sort(["month", "decile"])
)
```

```{python}
#| label: me_values
me_values = (
    msf
    .with_columns(
        mktcap=pl.col("prc").abs() * pl.col("shrout") / 1000,
        month=pl.col("date").dt.truncate("1mo"),
    )
    .select("permno", "date", "mktcap", "month")
    .filter(pl.col("month").dt.month() == 12)
)
```

```{python}
#| label: me_deciles
me_decile_assignments = (
    me_values
    .join(me_breakpoints, on=["month"], how="inner")
    .filter(
        pl.col("mktcap").is_between("me_min",
                                    "me_max", closed="left")
    )
    .with_columns(
        year=(pl.col("date").dt.year() + 1).cast(pl.Int32)
    )
    .select("permno", "year", "decile")
)
```

## Earnings news variables

:::{.callout-note}
The expressions `pl.col("earn", "cfo")`, `.era.div_if_pos("lag_at")`, and `.era.ntile(10)` keep the transformation pipeline concise while still working on lazy data.
:::

```{python}
#| label: news
#| cache: false
news = (
    funda
    .filter(
        pl.col("indfmt") == "INDL",
        pl.col("datafmt") == "STD",
        pl.col("consol") == "C",
        pl.col("popsrc") == "D",
        pl.col("fyr") == 12
    )
    .select(
        "gvkey",
        "datadate",
        "fyear",
        "at",
        pl.col("ibc").alias("earn"),
        pl.col("oancf").alias("cfo"),
    )
    .sort(["gvkey", "datadate"])
    .with_columns(
        lag_at=pl.col("at").shift(1).over("gvkey"),
        lag_fyear=pl.col("fyear").shift(1).over("gvkey"),
    )
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("earn", "cfo")
        .diff()
        .over("gvkey")
        .era.div_if_pos("lag_at")
        .name.suffix("_chg")
    )
    .filter(
        pl.col("fyear").is_between(1987, 2002),
        pl.col("lag_fyear") + 1 == pl.col("fyear")
    )
    .select("gvkey", "datadate", "earn_chg", "cfo_chg")
    .with_columns(
        (pl.col("earn_chg", "cfo_chg") > 0)
        .name.replace(r"_chg$", "_gn")
    )
    .filter(
        pl.all_horizontal(
            pl.col("cfo_gn", "earn_gn").is_not_null()
        )
    )
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("earn_chg", "cfo_chg")
        .era.ntile(10)
        .over("datadate")
        .name.replace(r"_chg$", "_decile")
    )
)
```

## Merge and plot

```{python}
#| label: merged
#| cache: false
merged = (
    news
    .with_columns(year=pl.col("datadate").dt.year())
    .join(rets, on=["gvkey", "datadate"], how="inner")
    .join(me_decile_assignments, on=["permno", "year"], how="inner")
    .with_columns(month=pl.col("date").dt.truncate("1mo"))
    .join(size_rets, on=["decile", "month"], how="inner")
    .drop(["permno", "month"])
)
```

:::{.callout-note}
The next step is where the lazy pipeline is finally materialized via `.collect()`.
:::

```{python}
#| label: plot_data
ret_cols = [
    c for c in merged.collect_schema().names()
    if c.endswith("ret")
]

plot_data = (
    merged
    .filter(pl.col("ret").is_not_null())
    .sort(["gvkey", "datadate", "rel_td"])
    .with_columns(
        **{
            c: pl.col(c).add(1).cum_prod().over(["gvkey", "datadate"])
            for c in ret_cols
        }
    )
    .group_by(["rel_td", "earn_gn"])
    .agg(**{c: pl.col(c).mean() for c in ret_cols})
    .with_columns(
        aret_ew=pl.col("ret") - pl.col("ew_ret"),
        aret_vw=pl.col("ret") - pl.col("vw_ret"),
        **{
            "Earnings news": pl.when(pl.col("earn_gn"))
            .then(pl.lit("Good"))
            .otherwise(pl.lit("Bad"))
        },
    )
    .sort(["earn_gn", "rel_td"])
    .collect()
)
```

:::{.callout-note}
The `p9()` context manager temporarily imports the `plotnine` names used in the plotting code.
:::

```{python}
#| label: fig-bb-1
#| fig-cap: "Replication of Figure 1 of Ball and Brown (1968)."
#| fig-alt: "Cumulative abnormal returns for good versus bad earnings news around annual earnings announcements."
with p9():
    fig = (
        ggplot(
            plot_data,
            aes("rel_td", "aret_ew",
                linetype="Earnings news", group="Earnings news"),
        )
        + geom_line()
        + theme_bw()
        + theme(legend_position="bottom")
    )

fig
```
